title: Introduction to Cybersecurity and Strategy
description: The CCMAS introduction to cybersecurity: basic concepts and the CIA triad, authentication and access control, security policies and best practices, security testing and incident response, software and hardware vulnerabilities and malware, and risk management and the impact of cyber attacks. Built from the CYB 201 lecture slides (Weeks One to Three) and the course notes in the folder.

topics.title: Cybersecurity Concepts and the CIA Triad
topics.summary: Cybersecurity is the practice of safeguarding computers, networks, software and data against unauthorized access and malicious activity in cyberspace. Its core objectives are the CIA triad of confidentiality, integrity and availability, each with standard protective measures.

topics.title: Authentication and Access Control
topics.summary: Authentication confirms the identity of a user, device or system before access is granted and is the first line of defence. Access control regulates who can enter a system and what they may do, through models such as discretionary, mandatory and role-based access control and the principle of least privilege.
subtopics: Authentication as the first line of defence
Role-based access control (RBAC) and least privilege

topics.title: Security Policies and Best Practices
topics.summary: Security policies set the standards, rules and procedures for using systems and protecting information. Types include enterprise, issue-specific and system-specific policies, and best practices cover encryption and backups, least privilege, passwords, network security, patching, audits, awareness training and recovery planning.
subtopics: Supplemental policies: network, data and acceptable use

topics.title: Security Testing and Incident Response
topics.summary: Security testing examines systems, networks and applications to find vulnerabilities before attackers do, through vulnerability testing, penetration testing, audits, risk assessment and ethical hacking. Incident response planning defines how to detect, contain, eradicate, recover from and learn from incidents.
subtopics: Goals and objectives of security testing
Security auditing, risk assessment and ethical hacking

topics.title: Vulnerabilities, Exploits and Malware
topics.summary: A security vulnerability is a software or hardware defect that attackers try to exploit; an exploit is a program written to take advantage of it. Software vulnerabilities include buffer overflow, non-validated input, race conditions, weak security practices and access-control problems, and malware includes spyware, adware, bots and ransomware.
subtopics: Malware: spyware, adware, bots and ransomware
Evolution and impact of attacks on systems

topics.title: Risk Management and the Impact of Cyber Attacks
topics.summary: Risk management looks at what could go wrong and decides how to prevent or limit it, through risk assessment, risk mitigation and evaluation. Cyber attacks affect systems, networks, organisations and civil institutions, so organisations plan for disaster recovery and business continuity.
subtopics: The three parts of risk management
Impact on civil institutions and their challenges
